The way I hear the tune the bar actually ends on the “e”:
|cAA d2 A e2|
Jack, I was a bit confused about using an underscore as I thought you were dealing with the slurring part. I should have known about the flat but it didn’t occur to me that you might actually be suggesting an e-flat in there.
I can’t remember the last time I had to add a flat accidental to notate a tune whereas sharps and naturals seem to happen quite often.
I am just so suprised that Dow came and went without pouring scorn on the tune with its silly syncopated bits. He would like it even less if he heard the risque chords I use accompanying this tune.
Swisspiper, I do tend to agree with you in that |cAAd - dA e2| is a much neater way of writing what I wrote above, and maintains the reel structure.

“Take A Message To Julie” C: Brian Finnegan

I haven’t heard the recording and am not familiar with this tune, but it did remind me of a couple of slow reels and that’s where I went with it, slowly and in a contemplative mind set ~ with visiting a few other places on the way.

I was just going to write it out with ‘lead-ins’ and not 1st and 2nd endings, which would allow the transcription to resolve where the tune goes ~ on E, for E Dorian, but ~ I got a little carried away ~ enjoying the tune and tickling it differently here and there, so here are some other possibilities with it, and me in a reflective mood ~
